_what: Seven Days to the Wolves — the whole programme, assembled from its acts. THE RUNNING ORDER IS CANONICAL and settled by the owner on 2026-08-12: intro (I) -> endlessformsmostbeautiful (II) -> mrbobbytables (III) -> kat (IV) -> nat (V) -> 7daystothewolves (VI) -> europa (VII) -> credits (VIII). docs/running-order.md is the source of truth for it; this file executes it.

_acts.0: PROLOGUE -- the main title sequence, and THE ONE ENTRY WITH NO NUMERAL. The eight act numerals are load-bearing (AGENTS.md: 'III is mrbobbytables permanently'), so a cold open in front of act I is numbered outside them rather than by renumbering everything behind it. Like act VIII it carries NO SLIDE AND NO CHAPTER MARKER: chapters() derives markers from slides, and a card announcing the main title sequence would step on the main title sequence. Picture is Nightwish's official 'Perfume Of The Timeless' music video -- see the rights note in music/bed_perfume_of_the_timeless.json, and stories/megacut/delivery.json for why it has no social copy.
_acts.I: intro — the Into the Light opener, six Guardians and companions plated beneath the owner-authored cinematic captions, ending on the Platform Wars card.
_acts.II: endlessformsmostbeautiful — five unbroken runs of the live-action trailers scored to Nightwish's Endless Forms Most Beautiful (instrumental); The Long Walk inside them. It is built by scripts/build_efmb.py. Its picture is a fan compilation (same provenance question as act VI, #55).
_acts.III: mrbobbytables — the August 2026 contributors piece, cut from the Curse of Osiris opening cinematic. Owner-named and owner-placed, and placed as-is: assembly never re-cuts what it is handed.
_acts.IV: kat — Kat Cosgrove's Guardian intro, behind the owner-authored BIAS FOR ACTION slide.
_acts.V: nat — Natali Vlatko's Guardian arrival, behind the same authorisation slide retitled WRONG PLACE, WRONG TIME, RIGHT ATTITUDE.
_acts.VI: 7daystothewolves — the musical. Provenance is unresolved (#55). Its tail plates the Cayde-6 reveal and three gold credits.
_acts.VIII: credits — the cast, 454 contributors across four projects, the comic-cover reveal at :22 and the Project Bluefin wordmark. The act that makes this the feature rather than seven eighths of it (#51).

_audio: Every act carries its own audio, unprocessed: no normaliser, no limiter, no EQ. The programme is 48 kHz STEREO because that is what the masters are -- every -hq master in Prod is stereo FLAC. Upmixing here would be assembly inventing a soundfield, which the audio tenet forbids; if 5.1 delivery is wanted, it belongs in the per-cut scripts that already do it. Only the six act slides are silent; a bed under them is a licensing decision.
_transitions: Fade shapes at the act joins. THE NUMBERS ARE NOT RESTATED HERE -- each clip carries its own `fade_in`/`fade_out`, in ACT FILM time (the clip's own clock), so a re-order never moves them and this note can never disagree with them. Read the items; re-measure with `python3 tools/transitions.py --measure` on the built programme rather than believing any paragraph. THE PRINCIPLE (#105): an act that fades itself out carries no `fade_out` -- doubling the taper on a fade the act already performs is the fault, not the fix. Acts II and VI fade themselves; the prologue runs itself down to -58.7 dB RMS across its last three seconds and act I opens at digital silence climbing through -30 to -18 dB, so that join carries no fade on either side. Where music meets music at full level the join is hard, per docs/skills/megacut/references/joins.md. A dip is right only where the incoming act enters QUIET. LEFT TO THE OWNER (automatable: no): levelling the act ENTRIES, which still differ by roughly 20 dB -- a static gain per act is a mix decision, not a derivation.

_sources._where: Every act plays from ~/Videos/Wolves/Prod, which holds the HIGHEST-QUALITY master of each: FLAC audio and the un-re-encoded picture. They are hardlinks to the per-project masters, so Prod costs no extra disk and cannot drift from what its project built.

_master_gain: -1.7 dB, measured on the DECODED deliverable and never asserted, landing the joined programme on the -1.0 dBTP house target. The programme is not asked to carry any act's headroom: a clipping act master is corrected AT SOURCE by tools/peaks.py trim (a derived static gain, picture stream copied), which is the hole issue #82 recorded -- a lossless master never gated because only the lossy copy ever was. Re-measure after every rebuild. No normalizer, limiter, compression or EQ, at any step.
_distribution_gain: -2.1 dB, applied to the LOSSY leg only: extra headroom the AAC copy needs and the lossless master does not. Measured on two outputs built from the SAME PCM segments with the same -1.7 mix gain -- the FLAC master read -1.1 dBTP and the AAC copy +1.0, inter-sample peaks the encoder reconstructs above the samples it was given. The copy re-measures at -3.2 dBTP / -13.9 LUFS. THAT IS 2.1 dB LOWER THAN THE ARITHMETIC PREDICTS, AND IT IS KEPT: tools/peaks.py records that the overshoot is NOT monotonic in the gain (measured elsewhere in this project: gain 0.658 delivered -2.5 dBTP while 0.675 delivered -0.8), so chasing a narrow window costs a full ten-minute encode per attempt and can land further out than it started. The rule is stop at the first SAFE result. Nothing is lost by being conservative: the quality reference is the lossless .mkv master, which sits on the house -1.1 dBTP band, and -13.9 LUFS integrated is within a tenth of YouTube's own -14 normalisation target, so the distribution copy plays back at the same loudness either way. Never a limiter, a normalizer, compression or EQ. Re-measure BOTH files after every rebuild.

items.label: Act VI — Seven Days to the Wolves: the musical, CUT ON THE LAST SHOT CHANGE (430.997) so the song hands straight to the next one and the closing flash never plays
items._needle_drop: Owner 2026-08-16: '22:38 work on this transition it's too janky.' MEASURED, and the jank is in the PICTURE, not the music: act VI's last 14 frames are a separate shot -- a pink tableau flashing to a dark Exo shot at act-film 430.997 -- so the programme played a quarter-second stinger nobody wrote and then cut songs. 430.997 is that shot change, and the out point sits on it, so the flash never starts. The needle drop is UNHARMED: movement 4 still opens on its own first hit, measured at +0.032 s past the seam against +0.035 before (spectral flux, 128-sample hop), and the post-seam audio of the two candidates cross-correlates at lag 0.00 ms, r = 0.997. WHAT IT COSTS, recorded because it is real: act VI's pickup accent at 431.075 goes with the flash, so the new song arrives without the three-strike cut-accent-drop figure the longer tail set up. Excerpts for all three candidates are at renders/review/join-2238-{A-asshipped,B-picturedissolve,C-shotchange}.mp4, 8 s each with the seam at 4.000 s. A keeps the flash. B dissolves the picture for 0.5 s and keeps the accent, but the blend smears the internal shot change into a visible three-way content swap (motion 20.3 mid-blend) and needs xfade support megacut.py does not have. C is this one.

items.label: Ending — the Project Bluefin mission, in silence
items._silence: Digital silence, generated to the programme layout rather than taken from the clip (the render carries no audio stream at all). No bed, no ambience, no loudness processing: the passage is silent BY DESIGN, and the audio tenet forbids adding anything to make it feel less empty. Built by scripts/build_ending_pause.py from stories/megacut/ending-cards.json -- 1380 frames at 60000/1001, five wallpaper cards with slow cross-fades and a short black tail.
items._not_an_act: Connective tissue, not an act: no Roman numeral, no slide, no chapter marker. The canonical act order in docs/running-order.md is unchanged.
items._seat: Owner 2026-08-16: 'when the jupiter scenes fade to black play the slideshow.' The passage follows act VII's own fade to black and precedes movement 5a. Its tail hold is 30 frames rather than the length a passage handing straight into the impact wants -- the reason is in ending-cards.json `_black_hold`: a near-black Earth limb follows it, and two darks stack.

items.label: Perfume, movement 5a — source 389.800 -> 393.560, the dark Earth limb before the impact
items._split: 5a and 5b are the same movement either side of one frame boundary at source 393.560, where the asteroid shot starts. Nothing is cut from the song. They now play back to back, so the boundary is inaudible by construction rather than by treatment -- but both files are KEPT SEPARATE, because 5b is the overlaid derivative carrying the closing lines and 5a is clean picture the dinosaur pass can still work on.
items._no_fade_in: NO fade in. 5a opens on a dark Earth limb (Y~24) that holds 3.504 s before the sun bursts over the curve (Y jumps to 93) -- the shot the owner calls 'the sun over the planet' and asked to hold until here. It now follows the slideshow's black rather than Europa's eclipse, so the song RE-ENTERS on this frame at full level after the silent passage. A fade under an already near-black shot would put the re-entry underwater; the song simply arrives, and 3.5 s later the sun pays it off.
items._thread: Movement 5 of 5, and the end of the song. The owner asked to 'match the transition panning up from laura after europa'. MEASURED, AND THE PREMISE DID NOT SURVIVE: there is no pan on either side. Europa's tail is the Europa/Jupiter vista behind the KubeCon card, fading to black, and movement 5 opens on a static dark Earth limb -- vertical displacement is 0 px across both, by row-profile correlation. What the join actually is, and what it is good at, is dark-to-dark: one world in space goes out, another comes up, and 3.5 s later the sun breaks over it. Act VII is never shortened to make anything FIT (#178) -- the trim on it is the owner's own eclipse note.
items._reordered: Owner 2026-08-16, the whole note in three parts: '26:08 this should have faded to black, save this scene for later, it's pivotal' / '26:08 when the jupiter scenes fade to black play the slideshow' / '26:34 NOW do the shot with the sun over the planet - you have it right you just have this section on the wrong side of the slidedeck - play the section that is currently in 26:08 from this point on.' So 5a MOVES BEHIND the silent mission passage. The seat is the only thing that changed: the window (389.800 -> 393.560), the trim and the picture are untouched, and the file is not re-rendered. WHAT IT BUYS ON THE SOUND: 5a and 5b are now ADJACENT, so the last 117 s of Perfume plays as one unbroken run and the silence sits in FRONT of it instead of splitting it in half. That is a fact about the audio and is verified on the built file; whether it plays better is the owner's reading, and it is the reading they asked for.

items.label: Perfume, movement 5b — source 393.560 onward: the impact, then the underwater passage and its seven lines
items._resume: Picture and source audio resume at source 393.560 with NO fade, so the asteroid transient arrives intact and the silence is broken by the impact rather than eased out of. The derivative is built directly from the original source at the same 389.800 in point as renders/perfume-5.mp4, so this trim_from is in the same timebase as the clean movement and its decoded audio is identical to it.
items._lines: The seven closing lines are burned into this derivative by scripts/build_ending_overlays.py, revealed one at a time over the underwater pullback (source 396.320 -> 427.440). The clean renders/perfume-5.mp4 keeps its own rule and carries no overlays. Copy and timing are authored in stories/megacut/ending-cards.json.
items._trim: Owner 2026-08-14 (alpha QA): '28:20 has extra fade out that can be cut, including the music video director text, transition when the camera is in the ship make the song fade out but not too much then punch them with the credits at the end.' MEASURED: 28:20 programme time is movement 5's own tail. The in-ship shot (camera inside the sunken wreck, light through the hull) dissolves out from ~109.5; the source's burned credits ('(c) A LOVELY BUNCH OF COCONUTS 2024 / DIRECTED BY VILLE LIPIAINEN') fade in from 111.0 and are readable by 111.5, then near-black, then a held interior to EOF at 117.221 -- there is no shot boundary >=0.15 after film 100, it is one long dissolve, so the point is chosen on the frames: 109.5 is the last moment the camera still reads as IN the ship, with zero text risk. trim_to 109.5 cuts all of it; the 1.5 s fade_out lands against the AUTHORED end (st 108.0), which is 'fade out but not too much' from a -20 dB mean bed; act VIII's fade_in stays 0.0 so the drum smash punches on the next frame. Cuts 7.7 s of programme.
items._moves_the_ambush: RESOLVED by the owner's 28:20 note (was TODO(owner)/#191): the ambush now lands off the in-ship shot at mid-energy -- a 1.5 s fade from a -20 dB bed, not the source's long decay into burned credits and near-black. The picture is still deliberately left un-faded in the RENDER (these movements are rendered clean for the dinosaur pass); the trim and fade live here in the plan where they can be read, tested and reverted.

items.label: Act VIII — Credits
items._what: NO ACT SLIDE, by owner instruction: 'no credits slide, go right to the metal ... it should surprise the viewer.' Every other act is announced by a card; this one is not. Europa fades to black on its own tail and the drum smash lands on the next frame. The missing slide also removes act VIII's CHAPTER MARKER -- chapters() derives them from slides -- and that is the point rather than a side effect: a 'VIII. Credits' entry on the scrub bar would spoil the same surprise the cut is built to land. fade_in is 0.0 so nothing eases in front of the smash.
items._hard_out: NO fade_out. Owner 2026-08-16: '35:50 this is almost perfect but cuts off too early ... hold the bluefin mark until the end of the song. We want the double bass drum climax.' The act now plays the song to its natural end: the ring decays to -75 dBFS at the last frame, measured on the delivered act. A 3 s fade over that is the very thing the note complains about -- it would take the climax away again, one bar later than before.

_chapters: Each act slide carries the audience-facing `chapter` title; `python3 tools/megacut.py <plan> --chapters` derives the timestamps from this plan's own clock, so the markers can never drift from the running order. The numeral is part of the title because the show is told in numbered acts. Which acts publish a marker is derived from which items carry a `chapter` key -- do not count them here. Act VIII carries none deliberately: a scrub-bar entry would spoil the ambush. Act VII carries none because the owner asked for its title slide to go so movement 4 could hard-cut into Europa, and the marker went with the slide. If Europa should keep a scrub-bar entry with no card in front of it, chapters() would need to read a `chapter` off the CLIP -- a change nobody has asked for.
